content: 1. Class I refers to conditions where there is robust evidence and/or a general consensus that a specific procedure or treatment is beneficial, useful, and effective. 2. Class II refers to conditions where there is conflicting evidence and/or differing opinions regarding the usefulness or efficacy of a particular procedure or treatment. 3. Class IIa indicates that the majority of evidence and/or expert opinion supports the usefulness or efficacy of the procedure or treatment. 4. Class IIb suggests that the usefulness or efficacy of the procedure or treatment is less well established based on available evidence and/or expert opinion. 5. Class III pertains to conditions where there is evidence and/or general agreement that a procedure or treatment is not useful or effective, and in some cases, may even be harmful. 6. Level of Evidence A is based on data derived from multiple randomized clinical trials or meta-analyses. 7. Level of Evidence B is based on data obtained from a single randomized trial or non-randomized studies. 8. Level of Evidence C is based solely on expert consensus, case studies, or standard-of-care practices.
